newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Parliament on Thursday passed two bills to bolster the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to protect the investors' interest effectively and efficiently.
Speaker Humayun Rashid Chowdhury on Wednesday appealed to all members of the parliament to uphold the "sanctity and image" of the House by maintaining courtsey.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday stressed the need for political stability in the country for economic development.
Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, now on a visit to Malaysia, on Wednesday discussed problems of Bangladeshi workers with his counterpart Dato Abdullah Bin Haji Ahmad Badawi in Kuala Lampur.
Opposition BNP Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Wednesday dubbed the Thakurgaon by-election as a "farce" and said it would remain as a bad instance in democratic practice.
Private recruiting agencies of the coutry are soo going to get permission to export manpower to Taiwan.
Establishment of the National Stock Exchange will make the country's capital market more transparent and accountable, Finance Minister S A M S Kibria told the parliament on Wednesday.
Purbachal Jute Industries Ltd, a state-owned jute mill, has been sold out to the Sidwal Textile of Hong Kong.
